findings.text: follow-on: the negative control does not isolate the tightened count. Its declared mutation makes every renew_producer_lease call a throttled no-op, which also lapses the producer's lease, so test_a_renewed_producer_outlives_three_lease_intervals fails at line 119 (thread.is_alive) before the new renewals >= 5 assertion at line 122 is reached. Reproduced by me: the same throttle-only mutation against the BASE test fails at the identical assertion (logs/applied-control-old-test.log), so the mutation reddens old and new alike and shows nothing about the counting change. An isolating control that also holds the producer up (watch_ticker._lease_remaining reduced to None) reaches the count and fails at line 122 with assert 0 >= 5 (logs/isolating-control-new-test.log), which is the demonstration the node's own control omits. The claim quoted in the fragment (the old non-None count would have read six) is accurate about the renewals >= 5 assertion in isolation, but the control log it cites does not evidence it because the run never reaches that line.

raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20261002T032210779037-lease-renewal-is-counted-by-its-writes
(plan a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner, section s3; reviewed node lease-renewal-is-counted-by-its-writes)
reviewed_base_sha: 3b883745b34d85fe612736519ded2a6ada178f25
reviewed_head_sha: 05c81f326d7542f5c286709019db0bb9cb3a0c1c

The change is test-only. tests/test_producer_holds_a_lease.py:96 counts a lease renewal
only when runs.watch_lease_renewed_at advances between calls, replacing a count of
runs.renew_producer_lease(...) is not None. reckon/crew/runs.py is unchanged (diff
3b883745b..05c81f326 over reckon/crew/runs.py is empty), so the throttled non-None return at
runs.py:1270-1271 is real: on a throttled pass renew_producer_lease hands back the existing
registration without writing lease_renewed_at (set only at seat-take runs.py:2035 and on a
landed renewal runs.py:1272). The old count therefore accepted a no-op as a renewal; the new
one requires an observed advance. I read the source and re-ran the head arm.

What I measured myself, in scratch trees under $TMPDIR (logs in this run's logs/), never in
the reviewed worktree:
- The node's own negative control, reproduced: base tree 3b883745b with renew_producer_lease
  reduced to a throttle-only body, run against the BASE test. It FAILS at
  tests/test_producer_holds_a_lease.py:110 (thread.is_alive), exactly as the node's control
  fails its head test at line 119. Both arms die on the producer's lapsed lease, before the
  count assertion is reached. logs/applied-control-old-test.log.
- An isolating control I added: the same throttle plus watch_ticker._lease_remaining reduced
  to None so the producer stays up. Under it the head test fails at line 122
  (assert 0 >= 5): the tightened count fires. logs/isolating-control-new-test.log.
  The base test under the same control fails later, at line 115 (advanced > fresh).

VERDICT goal: the node's goal is that the lease test count a renewal only when
lease_renewed_at moved, so renewals >= 5 measures writes. tests/test_producer_holds_a_lease.py:111-115
reads watch_lease_renewed_at after each renew_producer_lease call and increments only when
the instant strictly advances; the head arm passes 3/3. The goal is met.
VERDICT done_when: the done-when asks the file to count by observed changes of lease_renewed_at
rather than by a non-None return; the diff does exactly that, runs.py is untouched, and base and
head both pass 3/3 with zero added failures. Met.
VERDICT write_paths: the diff 3b883745b..05c81f326 lists exactly the test file, the new fragment,
and the re-measured producer-holds-a-lease fragment; all are inside the node's declared write
paths, nothing under reckon/ differs, and the worktree is unmodified at head with no held changes.
VERDICT manifest: read in full; it names both commits, the two arms as JSON with literal commands
and real log paths, the negative-control log, and resolved evidence_inputs. It is internally
consistent with the logs it cites.
VERDICT diff: read commit by commit. 363c96b38 is the test's counting change plus a mechanism
comment; 05c81f326 adds the new fragment and a re-measured paragraph to the existing fragment.
No test removed, no skip or xfail added, and the final write check (advanced > fresh) is kept.
CALL_SITES: none

SCORE goal_fidelity: 19
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the change does exactly what the done-when names, verified by reading
runs.py (renew returns the existing record on throttle) and re-running the head arm green; the
deduction of one is for the count conflating the follower's renewal writes with any writer that
advances lease_renewed_at, of which the producer's seat-take is the only one and it precedes the loop.
SCORE evidence: 15
JUSTIFICATION evidence: both arms are recorded with literal commands and real log paths, the arms
were pinned with -P in scratch trees, and zero added failures is derivable from the reviewed run's
own manifest; deducted because the node's negative control fails on the shared is_alive assertion
(line 119) rather than on the tightened renewals >= 5 assertion, so it does not show the new
counting is load-bearing, and my isolating control was required to reach that assertion.
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: every changed path lies inside the declared write paths, reckon/crew/runs.py
is identical between base and head, and the worktree is unmodified at head with no held changes.
SCORE durability: 18
JUSTIFICATION durability: the change is committed in two conventional commits and the evidence lives in
the fragment; the new count reads a value the test observes rather than a threshold that moves with the
code, and the floor of 5 is sound because only the first loop call can be throttled; deducted for the
new fragment lacking a trailing newline and for the control gap carried under evidence.
SCORE fit: 19
JUSTIFICATION fit: the edit follows the file's existing helper and comment idiom, the comment states the
mechanism (why a non-None return is not a write) rather than the task, and no plan, ticket or author
reference appears in the change.
